module_mood_contract: Preserves M3's unsettled competence by teaching when multi-agent decomposition is justified without resolving whether the synthesized output is trustworthy.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forcing function belongs in the prompt
rules_evaluated.evidence: This is a post-exercise lecture with no learner prompt or forcing function.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body teaches work, no cohort management
rules_evaluated.evidence: The body teaches workflow sizing, split criteria, and session-versus-subagent selection; cohort-management notes are outside the lecture body.
The lecture directly explains when and how to use the two multi-agent shapes demonstrated in the exercise.
The start-with-don't default preserves the intended M3 unease rather than presenting multi-agent output as unquestionably superior.
Separate sessions and subagents are explicitly grounded in the preceding retriever and stance exercises.
The lecture makes coordination cost, seams, and the risk of beige synthesis explicit.
It gives learners a practical test for questioning whether a split is genuinely needed.
It prepares learners to apply multi-agent patterns selectively in real work without promising three-times-better output.
House guidance is presented as a design judgment and does not invent evidence or practitioner claims.
The ending returns to the practical meta-frame: resist applying multi-agent to everything and keep the default small.
The lecture is explicitly placed after the exercise, so the pre-exercise constraint does not apply.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No cross-module sequencing inside reusable lecture
rules_evaluated.evidence: Phase references identify the two exercise shapes; the body does not require cross-module sequencing or manage later participation.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A slide's BODY is size-bounded, not just its header (§4's sibling).
rules_evaluated.evidence: No `##` slide chunks in the raw target; the one-slide-per-`##` body-size rule has no slide body to measure.
The title accurately describes the lecture's decision rule for splitting agents and choosing a shape.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Prompts in lectures are trainer demos only
rules_evaluated.evidence: Questions are rhetorical decision tests, not student-facing exercise prompts or cohort-management instructions.
